html:
Salamis was the main Greek city kingdom of ancient Cyprus, on the east coast north of today's Famagusta, founded around 1100 BCE after the decline of nearby Enkomi.

Its royal tombs of the 700s BCE held chariots and horses buried with the dead, as in Homer. Its king Evagoras, around 400 BCE, led a long revolt against Persia and spread Greek culture across the island. Under Rome it was the largest city of Cyprus, and the apostles Paul and Barnabas preached there; Barnabas was born there. Earthquakes in the 300s CE ruined it, and it was rebuilt as Constantia, capital of Christian Cyprus. Arab raids in 648 ended it, and the people moved to Famagusta.
sum: Salamis was the main Greek city kingdom of ancient Cyprus, on the east coast north of today's Famagusta, founded around 1100 BCE after the decline of nearby Enkomi.
